title: Eric Kang · Field Notes
tagline: Lessons learned firsthand: from engineering to leadership, building with AI, and the timeless wisdom of Eastern philosophy.
description: Practical notes from a career that went from electrical engineer at Motorola to Chief Knowledge Officer: moving from engineering into leadership, building AI-enabled services and agentic workflows, and what Eastern philosophy teaches about learning, growth, decision-making and living well.

author.name: Eric Kang
author.bio: Electrical engineer turned knowledge and AI strategy leader, working across Hong Kong, Malaysia and mainland China. Writes about moving into leadership, building AI-enabled services and agentic workflows, and lessons from Eastern philosophy.
about: I am Chief Knowledge Officer at Lifewood Data Technology, where I lead knowledge management, corporate affairs and business development, and help shape our AI strategy across Hong Kong, Malaysia and mainland China.

I trained as an electrical engineer (BSEE, Southern Illinois University; MBA, HKUST) and started my career as a design team leader at Motorola. Since then I have worked across business development, quality, data production and operations at Lifewood.

Here I write about what I have learned firsthand, from moving out of engineering into leadership to building AI-enabled services and agentic workflows. I also write about Eastern philosophy and the timeless lessons it offers anyone on learning, growth, decision-making and living well.
education: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
